verdict.summary: Standard Q8 finishes first by six answers, but the paired differences are not statistically significant. Treat the ordering as a local corroboration of the official direction, not proof that Standard is categorically better.
verdict.qualityConclusion: The three variants are statistically tied on this local run; Standard trades substantially higher TTFT for a small, uncertain quality edge.
verdict.publicationSafeClaim: On the complete 765-question RealWorldQA set, using the same local QVAC SDK/backend and exact option scoring, Standard Q8 scored 57.3% and both Flash variants 56.5%. Standard ranked first, but paired tests found no significant winner.

methodology.scoring: Exact multiple-choice option accuracy; one point per question; no cross-suite aggregation.
methodology.prompt: official question and options with answer-letter suffix
methodology.providerOrder: provider order rotates by case index
methodology.officialDifference: Tether reports a single VLMEvalKit harness and official benchmark metrics. This run matches the public dataset, checksum, option scoring, model quantizations and QVAC-native serving stack, but does not establish bit-for-bit parity of VLMEvalKit version, generation parameters, prompt template, image decoder/resize path, or hardware.

officialWeaknesses.localFinding: Not directly measurable: RealWorldQA has no reliable label isolating price/plate OCR.

officialWeaknesses.claim: Correct chart reading but incorrect aggregation
officialWeaknesses.localFinding: Not directly measurable in this scene-heavy RealWorldQA slice.
Observed directionally: only 3 explicitly labelled left/right cases; Standard passed 1 and each Flash passed 2. The sample is too small for a conclusion.
Not observable under one-letter constrained decoding; all 2,295 answers were parseable.
Not isolated by RealWorldQA capability labels; requires OCRBench/DocVQA/InfoVQA or a dedicated high-resolution OCR slice.
Not visible in aggregate here: Flash Q8 and Flash Q4 both scored 432/765, but each uniquely won 35 cases, so equal totals hide different errors.

promptAblation.conclusion: The VLMEvalKit prompt changes individual answers but produces no significant aggregate improvement on the controlled 120-case sample.

criticalities.title: Prompt and generation parity are not bit-for-bit proven
criticalities.risk: Small models can flip answers with formatting, option punctuation, image/text ordering, stop tokens and decoding settings.
criticalities.solutionA: Freeze and publish the exact local prompt/runtime configuration.
criticalities.solutionB: Run an A/B parity replication using the pinned upstream VLMEvalKit prompt and generation config.
criticalities.consequence: Without this, compare direction and distance cautiously; do not call the run an exact reproduction.

criticalities.title: Preprocessing differs intentionally between Standard and Flash
criticalities.risk: Standard consumes tiled/upscaled views while Flash consumes the native view; this is part of the model design but prevents attributing every difference to weights alone.
criticalities.solutionA: Keep official per-model preprocessing for product-realistic comparison.
criticalities.solutionB: Add a preprocessing ablation while retaining the official run as primary.
criticalities.consequence: Official preprocessing is the fair headline; the ablation explains whether tiling helps or hurts particular cases.

criticalities.title: RealWorldQA is compositionally imbalanced
criticalities.risk: Counting, spatial relation and binary reasoning contribute 518/765 questions, while several named capabilities have 1–3 cases.
criticalities.solutionA: Report only the overall official metric.
criticalities.solutionB: Report overall plus category denominators and suppress strong claims for tiny groups.
criticalities.consequence: Category percentages without denominators would look precise but be misleading.

criticalities.title: A single benchmark cannot validate all advertised capabilities
criticalities.risk: OCR, documents, charts, hallucination, instruction following and open-ended reasoning are weakly represented or absent.
criticalities.solutionA: Keep the claim strictly scoped to RealWorldQA.
criticalities.solutionB: Add official OCRBench, ChartQA, POPE and MM-IFEval replications later.
criticalities.consequence: The X post must not generalize this score to overall VisionPsy quality.

criticalities.title: Exact one-letter scoring masks answer quality
criticalities.risk: It measures option selection, not explanations, calibration, hallucination or repetition.
criticalities.solutionA: Use exact scoring because that is the benchmark metric.
criticalities.solutionB: Add a separate open-answer qualitative audit with a frozen rubric.
criticalities.recommended: A for benchmark; B as separate evidence
criticalities.consequence: Do not mix qualitative grades into the official accuracy denominator.

criticalities.title: The score gaps are statistically weak
criticalities.risk: Standard leads each Flash by 6/765, while paired exact McNemar p-values are about 0.70.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish counts, confidence intervals and paired tests together.
criticalities.consequence: The defensible conclusion is “no clear local winner”, despite the rank order.

criticalities.title: System resource KPIs are not model-isolated
criticalities.risk: macOS GPU counters are system-wide and unified memory/process RSS does not fully represent model footprint.
criticalities.solutionA: Show them as live operational telemetry.
criticalities.solutionB: Label their scope and avoid cross-machine claims; use isolated device profiling for publication-grade memory data.
criticalities.consequence: Latency is reliable for this machine/run; GPU/RAM comparisons need narrower claims.

criticalities.title: Equal aggregate scores can hide different failure sets
criticalities.risk: Flash Q8 and Q4 tie overall but disagree on 70 questions.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish paired disagreement counts and inspect recurrent clusters.
criticalities.consequence: The Q4 result does not prove quantization is lossless on individual cases.

criticalities.title: Official-number provenance changes with precision and table revision
criticalities.risk: FP32/model-card headlines and matching GGUF rows are not interchangeable.
criticalities.solutionB: Compare each local file only against its matching GGUF column and record source URLs/date.
criticalities.consequence: This avoids claiming a gain or loss against the wrong precision.

criticalities.title: No repeated-seed variance estimate
criticalities.risk: A deterministic run reveals paired case differences but not sensitivity to stochastic decoding or implementation nondeterminism.
criticalities.solutionB: Repeat a stratified subset and hash outputs/configuration.
criticalities.recommended: A for this exact benchmark; B for robustness audit
criticalities.consequence: One deterministic run is valid for the fixed protocol, not a universal variance estimate.

criticalities.title: Execution order is balanced but deterministically tied to case order
criticalities.risk: Each provider runs first, second and third exactly 255 times, but cyclic assignment can correlate with dataset ordering and case difficulty.
criticalities.solutionA: Keep cyclic rotation and report it.
criticalities.solutionB: Shuffle cases with a published seed, then apply a balanced Latin-square provider order.
criticalities.consequence: This run controls unequal position counts, but cannot cleanly estimate a causal cache/order effect from the position subsets.
